title: Danh Vo
subtitle: Ships that pass in the night
body:
Danh Vo’s work is inspired by the continual transformation observed while gardening on his farm north of Berlin. Plant cuttings entangled in fish bones and mushrooms sprouting from bronze bodies merge the living, the dead, and the inert in a singular sculptural vocabulary. His materials include calligraphy by his father and photography alongside marble, bronze, and ceramic fragments from diverse historical worlds. Through objects charged with symbolism—personal, historical, and cultural—Vo examines how meaning changes with context. Artists die and history forgets, yet, wood, marble, and bronze persist. Here, centuries-old objects marked by devotion, trade, migration, conflict, and intimacy enter into dialogue with newly made sculptures. Like ships that pass in the night, the objects gathered here meet only briefly: fragments from different centuries and continents, brought together by economic exchange, colonial conquest, and chance. In galleries that evoke the hold of a ship, they recall the long histories that carried them, and the passing encounters through which new meanings emerge.

Danh Vo: Ships that pass in the night is organized by The Shen Foundation in collaboration with the Art Gallery of Ontario. The exhibition is curated by Adam Welch, Carol and Morton Rapp Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, in collaboration with Kitty Scott, Director and Curator, at The Shen Foundation.

See the Art Gallery of Ontario website for further information.
